instruction: Open chamfer_plate.step. It is a 120 x 80 x 12 mm plate in source coordinates X=-60..60 mm, Y=-40..40 mm, Z=0..12 mm, with four through holes of diameter 5 mm centered at X=+/-25 mm and Y=+/-15 mm. Create an editable native FreeCAD 0.21.2 Path/CAM Job. Use G54 matching the source CAD coordinates: X0 Y0 at the plate center and Z0 at the plate bottom. Configure the stock as the complete 120 x 80 x 12 mm outer block. Use T2, an editable native chamfer ToolBit with CuttingEdgeAngle 90 degrees, to create one or more active native Deburr operations and no other cutting operations. Set Deburr Width to 0.500 mm and cover exactly the top outside contour and all four top hole mouths. Choose a valid tool diameter, tip diameter, nonnegative ExtraDepth, spindle speed, feed rates, direction, start points, and operation grouping as appropriate; the tool geometry and Deburr parameters must represent a physical 0.500 mm chamfer, and the tool-center radius for every hole-mouth path must remain positive. Each of the five boundaries must be machined as a complete closed contour. Retract above the Z=12 mm top face before any rapid XY move between disconnected contours, do not cut below the depth required by the 90 degree Deburr geometry, and leave no executable motion after program end. Use the native LinuxCNC postprocessor. Save the editable FreeCAD document and its matching postprocessed output using exactly these absolute paths: /home/user/Desktop/task-5.FCStd and /home/user/Desktop/task-5.nc.
